summary: B is the preferable base because it adds the required API with the established multipart helper and stays narrowly scoped. Neither patch fully satisfies the contract: both duplicate FilesService.Add instead of routing Upload through it, but A additionally makes a prohibited, SDK-wide retry/body-buffering change.
reasons: B adds the exact Upload signature and correctly uses multipartbody.NewFile("file", fileName, content), producing a replayable buffered body.
B preserves FilesService.Add and avoids changing global request and retry semantics.

A changes RawClient.Do to buffer nearly every io.Reader unless WithNoRetry is set. This affects unrelated endpoints, changes streaming and source-read timing, introduces memory risks, and directly conflicts with the instruction not to refactor unrelated retry machinery.

Both implementations duplicate Add's option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data error instead of calling s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), violating an explicit frozen contract requirement and creating maintenance drift.
risks_a: Global buffering may consume large or unbounded streams even when a request would not actually be retried.
The patch changes existing Add, Update, and arbitrary RawClient behavior beyond the requested convenience API.
Its extensive retry changes and documentation increase review surface for behavior the contract explicitly excludes.
risks_b: Upload must be changed to delegate to FilesService.Add rather than duplicating its internals.
The Upload test checks field name and filename but never reads and verifies the uploaded content.
It lacks required Upload-level tests for retrying streamed content, empty filename, nil content, source-reader errors, and FilesOption propagation, and the exported method lacks a Go doc comment.
